However, that said, your interpretation seems to be pretty close. You mention my artistic nature, my love of creating beauty and that is certainly true. Unlike other members of my family, I am very interested in how things look around me, and spend a lot of time decorating and organizing my environment. I also used to write creatively, draw and paint when I was younger and I would like to get back to myself. You also spend a lot of time talking about drawing on my experiences, my intelligence and my ability to think critically which I do believe to be true. You said my 4th decade, which is odd because I just started my fifth. But, I feel like I have packed a whole lot of experiences into those years. I also am college educated, and try to sort through information to reach a logical conclusion. Yet, you also talk about leading with my heart, which I am afraid I am often too prone to doing. Overall, it seemed a good and accurate reading. But, not sure why you said 4th decade when I know I gave you my birthdate. I'm turning 51 in April.

items.title: Free Trial Fraud at Its Most Shameless
items.text: This app offers a measly 3-day trial, which I naturally signed up for to see what the app had to offer—only to find that most features are still barred from usage unless you pay an additional fee for each specific component. A feature as simple as a birth chart reading requires a $20 payment. It even has a tab labeled "Free," which shows the limited content you're relegated to. So, it seems like the “trial” wasn't free at all—just a blatant ploy to get users to sign up in hopes they forget to cancel in time. At least other apps usually have the decency to unlock full premium access for a few minutes during the trial period. I can't even imagine what the basic version of this app is like, and frankly, I don't even want to check out what's available. I'm completely put off by such brazen greed—and that's saying a lot, considering most apps nowadays are pay-to-click by default.

We deserve to treat ourselves. That we are perfect the way we are. —————— —————— Okay, so this app gets super honest about all kinds of aspects about yourself, and it may feel really awful when it brings up the bad qualities, and at first I was hesitant to believe it, but this month it has been talking about how I will look at things in different perspectives, and that this month (October 2022) is best for observation, focus, and resolve. It takes a lot of resolve and insight to work on the negative parts of yourself, and to even accept them, but if you truly want to work on yourself, it can happen, and it can be done in a way that is patient and compassionate towards yourself and other people. This app has really helped me in these areas. I have a hard time listening to my positive qualities too, cause my entire life different people tried to stifle the good parts about me, so I am learning to hear good things about myself without feeling bad about it and actually accepting it. It is really nice how the app talks about how I can be creative and do really great things with my creativity if I put the work into it. items.title: An error right away?
items.text: So my birthday is August 23rd, which I know is on a cusp. However, in the app it says August 23rd is a Virgo, yet it says I am a Leo in the app. I understand the whole cusp thing gives me qualities of both, but in the app it lists the beginning of Virgo as August 23rd, but yet it categorizes me as a Leo, which ends the 22nd? I definitely listed my birthday correctly. I don't understand why it would categorize me as a Leo, when even in the app it begins Virgo on the 23rd? Is it a fluke? If you're going to categorize me as a Leo, then at least change the dates you categorize with so there is at least an explanation. Don't categorize me as a Leo, but then say Virgos start on the 23rd when you won't even categorize me as a Virgo. As for the app itself. The daily horoscopes are nice and even though it categorized me as a Leo instead of a Virgo, I was happy that I could still view the Virgo horoscope. As for the other features, you would have to pay to get anything else out of the app. Yes you get a free compatibility report, just one, if you wanted to try another you'd have to subscribe and pay. Honestly, I wish I could get past the Leo/Virgo issue I had, but it really bothers me and I think I'm going to have to delete the app. Please update your dates or fix the issue of having August 23rd-ers categorized as Leos when even in the app it says August 23rd is a Virgo.

items.title: "Insightful and Thought-Provoking"
items.text: I recently had the opportunity to explore the Nebula astrology app, and I must say that it left a lasting impression. As someone who appreciates both spirituality and self-discovery, I found Nebula to be a valuable companion on my journey. Nebula doesn't just provide generic horoscopes; it delves deeper. The personalized birth chart readings were remarkably accurate. It felt like the app had peeked into my soul, revealing aspects of my personality and life path that resonated profoundly. Whether you're a seasoned astrology enthusiast or a curious beginner, Nebula's insights are worth exploring. As with any form of divination, skepticism is healthy. Nebula acknowledges this delicate balance. It doesn't claim to have all the answers, but it encourages introspection. Rather than spoon-feeding predictions, it nudges you to consider possibilities. And that's where the magic lies—when you blend cosmic wisdom with your own discernment. Nebula doesn't promise to change your fate overnight. Instead, it reminds us that we're the architects of our destiny. The planets may influence, but our choices steer the ship. It's like having a celestial GPS—guidance without coercion. So, yes, Nebula offers insights, but it also empowers us to take charge. Beyond the charts and interpretations, Nebula fosters a sense of community. Connecting with like-minded souls, sharing experiences, and learning from one another—it's a cosmic coffee shop where the universe serves wisdom in every cup. In a world where noise often drowns out whispers of the stars, Nebula stands out. It's not about blind faith; it's about embracing the mystery. So, whether you're navigating life's storms or basking in its sunsets, Nebula is a worthy companion—one that encourages growth, reflection, and stargazing.
